title: Mr F & Forestry Appeals Committee
text:
Decision
Mr F & Forestry Appeals Committee
From
Office of the Commissioner for Environmental Information (OCEI)
Case number: OCE-300057-A0A2V8
Published on 9 June 2026
Background
Scope of Review
Decision
Appeal to the High Court
Whether the FAC had taken sufficient steps to identify and locate the relevant environmental information within the scope of the appellant’s request in accordance with article 7(5) of the AIE Regulations.
09 June 2026
Background
1. On 19 June 2025, the appellant requested the following information from the FAC:
“Information which has informed the FAC's consideration that the rules around State Aid and the associated payment of afforestation scheme grants and premiums are outside the remit of the FAC
.
To include any legal advice sought and received.
Please interpret this request broadly.
Please provide a schedule of records with your decision.
Please ensure that all records provided are compatible with Assistive Technology.
Could you please provide an acknowledgement of this request and contact details for the party assigned to deal with it.”
2. On 17 July 2025, the FAC issued its original decision to part grant the request. Following examination of material held by the FAC administration and the FAC committee the below records were considered relevant to the request:
• Agriculture Appeals Act 2001
• the Forestry Appeals Committee Regulations 2020 and the amending legislation. Both of which are available in the public domain on [external-link https://www.irishstatutebook.ie/ | https://www.irishstatutebook.ie/ ]
3. It also stated that “In the examination and search of material held by the FAC administration and the FAC committee I searched the following terms “Legal Advice”, “Legal Advice State Aid”
. These searches returned no records relevant to your request.” It included a schedule of records.
4. The FAC issued its internal review decision on 15 August 2025 affirming its original decision. That decision was appealed to this Office on 20 August 2025. The Commissioner issued his decision remitting this appeal
OCE-161673-J5Y3R0
on 14 November 2025, on the basis that the FAC had failed to demonstrate that it had taken sufficient steps to determine that it did not hold environmental information relevant to the appellant’s request.
5. The FAC issued its new internal review decision affirming its previous decisions on 30 January 2026. The appellant appealed the new internal review decision to this Office on 3 February 2026.
6. I have now completed my review under article 12(5) of the Regulations. In carrying out my review, I have had regard to the submissions made by the appellant and the FAC. In addition, I have had regard to:
a. the Guidance document provided by the Minister for the Environment, Community and Local Government on the implementation of the AIE Regulations (the Minister’s Guidance);
b. Directive 2003/4/EC (the AIE Directive), upon which the AIE Regulations are based;
c. the 1998 United Nations Economic Commission for Europe Convention on Access to Information, Public Participation in Decision-Making and Access to Justice in Environmental Matters (the Aarhus Convention); and
d. The Aarhus Convention—An Implementation Guide (Second edition, June 2014) (‘the Aarhus Guide’).
Scope of Review
7. In accordance with article 12(5) of the AIE Regulations, mr role is to review a public authority’s internal review decision and to affirm, annul or vary it. Where appropriate in the circumstances of an appeal, I will require the public authority to make available environmental information to the appellant.
8. The scope of this appeal concerns whether the FAC was justified in refusing access to environmental information on the grounds that no further information was held by or for the authority concerned in the meaning of article 7(5) of the Regulations.
Analysis and Findings
Article 7(5) of the AIE Regulations
9. Article 7(5) of the AIE Regulations is the relevant provision to consider, where the question arises as to whether the requested environmental information or any further environmental information is held by or for the public authority concerned. It provides as follows:
“Where a request is made to a public authority and the information requested is not held by or for the authority concerned, that authority shall inform the applicant as soon as possible that the information is not held by or for it”.
10. This Office’s approach to dealing with this type of case is to assess whether adequate steps have been taken to identify and locate relevant environmental information, having regard to the particular circumstances. In determining whether the steps taken are adequate in the circumstances, a standard of reasonableness is applied.
11. Article 7(5) of the AIE regulations allows a public authority to refuse a request if it does not hold the requested information. In order for a public authority to successfully rely on this provision, it must, among other things, provide evidence that it carried out adequate searches for the environmental information requested.
12. In its fresh internal review decision, the FAC provided an overview of the searches undertaken, which detailed the following:
“Following this extensive search, I can confirm that the FAC does not hold any separate documents, legal advice, or internal reports that specifically inform the Committee’s position that State Aid rules are outside its remit. Consequently, I must refuse the portion of your request seeking such advice or internal documents under Article 7(5) of the AIE Regulations, on the basis that the information is not held by or for the public authority.
To ensure a comprehensive response to your request, I have undertaken a new and extensive search of the Forestry Appeals Committee’s (FAC) records. My objective was to identify if any internal memo, legal opinions, or correspondence exist that contains the FAC’s remit in the context of State Aid. I conducted searches of both physical and electronic records held by the FAC Administration and the FAC Committee. This included the FAC’s electronic filing system (specifically folders relating to "Governance," "Legislation," and "Appeals Policy") and the archived email records.”
In order to capture any relevant documents that might not be explicitly labelled "Legal Advice," I searched using a broad range of keywords and combinations, including: "State Aid", "Remit", "State Aid", "Jurisdiction", "Grants", "Competition Rules", "Legal Opinion".
I consulted directly with the administrative team of the FAC to make sure if any external legal advice had ever been received on this specific topic, or if any internal guidance documents regarding State Aid rules had been drafted. I also examined general administrative folders to ensure no relevant records were misfiled or overlooked. While I have confirmed that no specific records exist, I wish to assist you by explaining the basis for the FAC’s position, as this answers your inquiry regarding what "informs" the FAC's consideration. The FAC is a statutory body established by legislation. Its functions and remit are derived strictly and exclusively from the text of the Agriculture Appeals Act 2001 (as amended) and the Forestry Appeals Committee Regulations 2020. The FAC does not hold a separate interpretation document or legal advice explaining its remit; rather, it relies directly on the statutory provisions contained within these Acts.
Therefore, the only "information" held by the FAC that informs its consideration on this matter is the legislation itself. As previously noted, these documents are in the public domain:
• Agriculture Appeals Act 2001
• Forestry Appeals Committee Regulations 2020
These can be accessed via the Irish Statute Book (www.irishstatutebook.ie). I am satisfied that I have taken all reasonable steps to locate the records you requested. I have verified through electronic searches and direct consultation that the FAC holds no further information, legal advice, or internal documentation relevant to your query regarding State Aid remit, other than the public legislation cited above.”
13. In all the circumstances, in particular the FAC’s explanation regarding the searches undertaken and the personnel who conducted the searches, I am satisfied that it has taken sufficient steps to determine that it does not hold any further records. I say this noting the FAC’s explanation that it relies directly on the statutory provisions contained within the legislation itself - Agriculture Appeals Act 2001, and Forestry Appeals Committee Regulations 2020 - both of which are in the public domain.
14. The FAC stated in its submission to this Office that it was satisfied that its refusal under Article 7(5) of the AIE Regulations is appropriate and justified. In response to the specific points raised by the appellant, it provided clarifications on what it described as the comprehensive nature of its search. It stated that “the FAC does not have a records destruction policy. Our practice is to retain all records, including emails, indefinitely. Therefore, no information relevant to the request could have been deleted.” It is not a function of this office to supervise, oversee or regulate the internal administrative practices or data retention policies of public authorities. Rather, the jurisdiction of this Office is confined to determining, in any particular case, whether information is held, or is not held by a public authority.
15. The FAC clarified that the search process involved consultation with “all relevant personnel.”
It stated that “This included the Chairperson, all Committee members, and the entire administrative team. Searches were run across the individual email accounts of every committee member and the central FAC administrative mailbox. We performed full text searches across the FAC's entire electronic filing system, not just specific folders. Searches used a broad range of keywords, including partial matches and variations e.g., "State Aid," "Remit," "Jurisdiction".”
16. The AIE Regulations do not require absolute certainty as to the existence or location of records. It is also important to note that the Commissioner does not generally expect public authorities to carry out extensive or indefinite general searches for records simply because an applicant asserts that more records should or might exist, or rejects a public authorises explanation of why a record does not exist. The test set out in article 7 (5) of the AIE Regulations is whether the public authority has taken all reasonable steps to locate the record(s) sought.
17. Article 7(5) of the AIE Regulations does not require a forensic trawling exercise to be conducted by public authorities, rather a test of reasonableness and an adequate search exercise should be performed. I am satisfied in this situation that adequate searches have taken place.
18. I am satisfied that on this occasion the FAC has taken sufficient steps to determine that it does not hold further environmental information relevant to the appellant’s request. Accordingly, the FAC was justified in refusing the request based on article 7 (5) of the AIE Regulations.
Decision
19. Having carried out a review under article 12(5) of the AIE Regulations, I affirm the FAC’s decision.
Appeal to the High Court
20. A party to the appeal or any other person affected by this decision may appeal to the High Court on a point of law from the decision. Such an appeal must be initiated not later than two months after notice of the decision was given to the person bringing the appeal.
Ger Deering
Commissioner for Environmental Information
